title: [01] Repo scaffold, tooling, quality gates
body:
## Why

Five quality gates enforced from the first commit. Retrofitting architectural
contracts onto code that already violates them means either a large refactor or a
pile of exemptions that defeat the purpose.

## Steps

**a.** `uv init` and copy `pyproject.toml` from the Setup wiki page verbatim. Do
not trim the dependency list — the pins are deliberate (`numpy>=2.0,<3` because
hdbscan, umap and lightgbm each lag NumPy majors).

**b.** Create the package layout under `src/linking_engine/`:
```
api/  models/  ingest/  embedding/  graph/  audit/  anchor/  discovery/  ml/  pipeline/
```
Each gets an `__init__.py`. `graph/` gets two files, `repo.py` and
`algorithms.py` — the split is enforced by contract, not convention.

**c.** Copy `.importlinter` to the repo root. Five contracts; the load-bearing one
is `algorithms-are-pure`, which forbids `graph.algorithms` from importing `neo4j`.

**d.** Add `.pre-commit-config.yaml` running ruff check, ruff format, and mypy on
staged files. Leave deptry and lint-imports to CI — they need the whole tree.

**e.** Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
```yaml
- uv sync --all-extras
- uv run ruff check
- uv run ruff format --check
- uv run mypy --strict src/
- uv run deptry src/
- uv run lint-imports
- uv run pytest
```

**f.** Create one trivial test so `pytest` exits 0 rather than "no tests
collected", which some CI configs treat as failure.

**g.** `.env.example` with every key the app reads, no real values. `.env` in
`.gitignore`.

## Acceptance

- `uv sync && uv run pytest` passes on a clean clone
- All five gates pass on an empty codebase
- `uv run lint-imports` reports 5 contracts kept

## Gotchas

- Python 3.14 is not yet supported by the ML tree. Pin `>=3.12,<3.14`.
- `asyncio_mode = "auto"` is already in the pytest config — async tests need no
  decorator, and forgetting one is a silent skip.

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [02] Pydantic domain models
body:
## Why

Models are the only thing crossing module boundaries. Every other rule in the
codebase depends on this holding.

## Steps

**a.** `models/enums.py`:
```python
class ActionType(StrEnum):
    ADD_LINK = "ADD_LINK"
    REANCHOR = "REANCHOR"
    REMOVE = "REMOVE"
    FIX = "FIX"
    CONTENT_GAP = "CONTENT_GAP"

class AnchorType(StrEnum):
    EXACT = "EXACT"; PARTIAL = "PARTIAL"
    NATURAL = "NATURAL"; BRANDED = "BRANDED"

class IssueFlag(StrEnum):
    GENERIC = "GENERIC"; MISALIGNED = "MISALIGNED"
    OFF_TOPIC = "OFF_TOPIC"; OVER_OPTIMISED = "OVER_OPTIMISED"
    WASTED_EQUITY = "WASTED_EQUITY"; BROKEN = "BROKEN"
    REDIRECTED = "REDIRECTED"; NOFOLLOW = "NOFOLLOW"
    NOINDEX_TARGET = "NOINDEX_TARGET"

class LifecycleStage(StrEnum):
    NEW = "NEW"; EMERGING = "EMERGING"
    ESTABLISHED = "ESTABLISHED"; MATURE = "MATURE"
```

There is deliberately **no REPOSITION**. The crawler extracts body links only, so
there is no footer to move a link out of.

**b.** `models/page.py` — `Page`, `Keyword`, `Link`. Every model:
```python
model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
```
`extra="forbid"` catches a renamed field at the boundary instead of silently
dropping it. `frozen=True` because these represent fetched or computed state.

**c.** `models/audit.py` — `LinkAuditResult` with all six scored dimensions
(`anchor_quality`, `keyword_alignment`, `context_relevance`, `anchor_target_fit`,
`equity_efficiency`, plus `issue_flags`), each `Field(ge=0, le=1)` except
`anchor_quality_score` which is `ge=0, le=100`.

**d.** `models/features.py` — `PairFeatures`, roughly 30 fields. Group by comment
block: GSC, lifecycle, strategic, target structural, source structural, cluster,
semantic. Use `float | None` for GSC fields, since new pages have no data, and add
an explicit `has_gsc_data: bool` so the model can distinguish missing from zero.

**e.** `models/recommendation.py` — `Recommendation` and `AnchorCandidate`.
`AnchorCandidate.source` is `Literal["EXTRACTED", "GENERATED"]`; post-v5 it should
always be EXTRACTED, but the field stays so acceptance can be tracked separately
if that changes.

**f.** `models/tenant.py` — `TenantConfig` via `pydantic-settings`, with the
defaults from the Data Model wiki page.

## Acceptance

- `mypy --strict` clean with `disallow_any_explicit` on this package
- Round-trip test: model → `model_dump()` → model, for each type
- A test asserting `extra="forbid"` actually raises on an unknown field

## Gotchas

- Use `HttpUrl` for urls, but note it normalises — `/foo` and `/foo/` may differ.
  Canonicalise before constructing, not after.
- `frozenset` for `issue_flags`, not `set` — models are frozen and `set` is not
  hashable.

**Depends on:** #1

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [03] Neo4j and Mongo repos, schema migrations, vector indexes
body:
## Why

`graph/repo.py` is the only module permitted to talk to Neo4j. That boundary is
enforced by `.importlinter`, and everything downstream assumes it.

## Steps

**a.** `graph/repo.py` — async driver with a module-level singleton and pooling:
```python
driver = AsyncGraphDatabase.driver(uri, auth=(u, p), max_connection_pool_size=50)
```
Expose typed methods returning Pydantic models. Never leak a `Record`.

**b.** Migration runner. Read `.cypher` files from `migrations/` in filename
order, track applied ones in a `(:_Migration {name, appliedAt})` node, run each
inside its own transaction. All statements must be idempotent — `IF NOT EXISTS`
on every constraint and index.

**c.** `migrations/001_schema.cypher` — constraints on `Page.url` and
`(Keyword.text, Keyword.language)`, plus indexes on `topic`, `isIndexable`,
`lifecycleStage`, `linkCommunityId`, `keywordCommunityId`, and on `LINKS_TO`
`auditedAt` and `anchorType`.

**d.** `migrations/002_vectors.cypher`:
```cypher
CREATE VECTOR INDEX page_content IF NOT EXISTS
  FOR (p:Page) ON p.content_embedding
  OPTIONS { indexConfig: {
    `vector.dimensions`: 2048,
    `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine' }};
```
Same for `page_gnn`.

⚠️ **Dimension is fixed at creation.** Changing it later means dropping the index,
re-embedding every page, and retraining the GNN. 2048 is chosen because Matryoshka
makes downgrading to 1024 a truncation of data already held, while upgrading needs
a full re-embed — take the reversible direction.

**e.** `ingest/mongo_repo.py` with `motor`. Every collection is tenant-scoped and
every compound index leads with `tenantId`. Connection string needs
`?directConnection=true` against a single-node replica set.

**f.** Startup health check: assert Neo4j version ≥ 5.18 by calling
`RETURN vector.similarity.cosine([1.0,0.0],[1.0,0.0])` and failing loudly if it
errors.

## Acceptance

- `testcontainers` spins real Neo4j and Mongo; migrations apply twice with no error
- `SHOW INDEXES` reports both vector indexes at 2048 dimensions
- Repo methods return Pydantic models, verified by mypy

## Gotchas

- Neo4j internal ids are **not stable** across restarts or deletions. Fine as a
  within-run mapping, dangerous cached.
- Mongo needs the replica set for transactions. Without `directConnection=true`
  the driver tries to discover other members and hangs with no useful error.

**Depends on:** #2

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [04] Voyage client: token-aware batching and backoff
body:
## Why

Batching by list length fails on long pages and wastes headroom on short ones.
voyage-4-large caps at **120,000 tokens per request** — not 1M, which is the lite
models. Getting this wrong means the first real run errors out mid-corpus.

## Limits

```
model              voyage-4-large
output_dimension   2048
input_type         document      everything here is a document, no query side
max per request    120,000 tokens
max list length    1,000
rate limits        3M TPM / 2000 RPM
```

At ~3,300 tokens per page that is roughly **36 pages per call**.

## Steps

**a.** `embedding/voyage_client.py` wrapping the SDK. Config from
`pydantic-settings`, never hardcoded.

**b.** Token-aware batcher:
```python
async def token_batches(texts, budget=110_000, max_items=1000):
    batch, total = [], 0
    for t in texts:
        n = vo.count_tokens([t])[0]
        if total + n > budget or len(batch) >= max_items:
            yield batch
            batch, total = [], 0
        batch.append(t); total += n
    if batch:
        yield batch
```
110K not 120K, for headroom against token-count drift.

**c.** Retry with `tenacity` — exponential backoff, jitter, retry on 429 and 5xx,
never on 4xx other than 429. This is per-call backoff *inside* a task; Prefect
retries whole tasks, which is a different granularity.

**d.** Always pass `input_type="document"`. There is no query side anywhere in
this pipeline — Step ④ is page-to-page and Step ⑦ is phrase-to-page. Getting this
backwards costs retrieval quality silently.

**e.** L2 normalise before returning. Neo4j's cosine index assumes unit vectors.
Voyage returns normalised by default, but assert it rather than trusting it —
`output_dtype="int8"` would change that.

**f.** Emit a metric per batch: token count, item count, latency, retry count.

## Acceptance

- Unit test with a mocked client proves no batch exceeds 110K tokens
- A 5,000-token page and a 200-token page batch correctly together
- 429 triggers backoff and eventually succeeds
- Returned vectors have norm 1.0 ± 1e-6

## Gotchas

- `count_tokens` needs `pip install tokenizers` — already in the manifest.
- Rate limit is per minute across all requests. At 25k pages the run takes ~28
  minutes and you *will* hit it; backoff must work, not just exist.

**Depends on:** #2

**Estimate:** 1.5 days

title: [05] Embedding write path with crash resume
body:
## Why

A run that dies halfway must leave a **consistent prefix**, not a half-written
index. And a partially populated HNSW index returns plausible-looking candidates
from an incomplete pool with no error at all — the failure is silent.

## Steps

**a.** Decouple the API batch from the DB write. Accumulate ~500 pages in a
buffer, then flush in a single `UNWIND`. Writing 36 rows at a time means 700 round
trips on a 25k-page corpus.

**b.** Write vector, hash, model and timestamp in the same transaction:
```cypher
UNWIND $rows AS r
MATCH (p:Page {url: r.url})
SET p.content_embedding    = r.vec,
    p.embeddedContentHash  = r.hash,
    p.embeddingModel       = $model,
    p.embeddedAt           = datetime()
```

**c.** Resume query — only embed what changed:
```cypher
MATCH (p:Page)
WHERE p.embeddedContentHash IS NULL
   OR p.embeddedContentHash <> p.contentHash
RETURN p.url
```

**d.** Mixed-model guard, run at startup:
```cypher
MATCH (p:Page) WHERE p.content_embedding IS NOT NULL
RETURN count(DISTINCT p.embeddingModel) AS models
```
More than 1 means two vector spaces in one index. **Fail the run.** Cosine between
vectors from different models is meaningless, and nothing else will tell you.

**e.** Progress logging every flush: pages done, remaining, tokens spent, elapsed.

**f.** Cap the buffer. 25k pages at 2048d float32 is ~200 MB held in Python before
anything is durable. 500–1000 is the right window.

## Acceptance

- Kill the process mid-run; rerun embeds only the remainder
- Editing one page's body re-embeds exactly that page
- Mixed `embeddingModel` values cause a startup failure with a clear message
- Memory stays flat across a full run

## Gotchas

- `contentHash` must be computed over the same text you embed. Hash the body you
  send, not the raw HTML.
- Do not put the resume check inside the batch loop — one query up front.

**Depends on:** #3, #4

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [06] Anchor and surrounding-sentence embeddings, deduplicated
body:
## Why

Feeds `contextRelevance` and `anchorTargetFit`. Naively embedding every edge means
250k texts; deduplication usually cuts that to a few thousand.

## Steps

**a.** Collect unique anchor strings across all `LINKS_TO` edges:
```python
unique = {normalise(l.anchor_text) for l in links}
```
Anchor text repeats heavily — `"click here"` might appear 400 times.

**b.** Skip anything the generic dictionary already flags. Its verdict is decided;
an embedding adds nothing.

**c.** Embed the unique set, then map back to edges by normalised string.

**d.** Surrounding sentences are mostly unique, so dedupe by `(source_url,
content_hash, sentence_index)` instead and cache across runs — an unchanged page
has unchanged sentences.

**e.** Write `surroundingEmbedding` onto the relationship. Note there is **no
relationship vector index** in Neo4j Community, so this cannot be ANN-searched.
Fine — the audit scans edges sequentially and uses
`vector.similarity.cosine()` directly.

## Acceptance

- Deduplication ratio logged; expect roughly 8k unique from 250k edges
- Same anchor text on different edges yields the identical vector
- Relationship property round-trips through the driver

## Gotchas

- Normalise before deduplicating — `"Click Here"`, `"click here "` and
  `"click here"` are one string for this purpose.
- Sentence embeddings are `input_type="document"`. A sentence is corpus text being
  matched, not a search query.

**Depends on:** #5

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [07] igraph backend: edge pull, id mapping, graph construction
body:
## Why

Algorithms run in-process, not in Neo4j GDS. That removes the 4-core Community
cap, the 3-projection limit, and JVM cache-miss overhead on BFS — which dominates,
since betweenness is 6.25 billion edge visits at 25k nodes and BFS is pure pointer
chasing. Contiguous int32 adjacency arrays keep the prefetcher fed; heap pointers
do not.

Result: graph analytics drops from ~50 min to 2–4 min.

## Steps

**a.** `graph/algorithms.py` must not import `neo4j`, `motor` or `pymongo`. This
is enforced by `.importlinter`. Algorithms take edge lists and return arrays;
only `graph/repo.py` speaks Bolt.

**b.** Edge pull in the repo layer, returning integer ids:
```cypher
MATCH (a:Page)-[:LINKS_TO]->(b:Page)
RETURN id(a) AS s, id(b) AS t
```
Integer ids, not URLs — igraph wants contiguous integers and string keys are far
slower.

**c.** Build a dense mapping. Neo4j ids are sparse, igraph needs `0..n-1`:
```python
node_ids = sorted({s for s, _ in rows} | {t for _, t in rows} | all_page_ids)
to_dense = {nid: i for i, nid in enumerate(node_ids)}
edges = [(to_dense[s], to_dense[t]) for s, t in rows]
g = ig.Graph(n=len(node_ids), edges=edges, directed=False)
```
Include isolated pages in `node_ids` — orphans must exist in the graph with degree
zero, or they silently drop out of every result.

**d.** ⚠️ **Rebuild the mapping every run.** Neo4j internal ids are not stable
across restarts or after deletions. Never cache it.

**e.** Undirected for Leiden and betweenness; keep a directed copy for PageRank,
since link direction genuinely matters for authority flow.

**f.** Log construction cost: rows fetched, build seconds, node and edge counts.

## Acceptance

- 250k edges pull and build in under 30 seconds
- Orphan pages appear in the graph with degree 0
- `lint-imports` confirms `algorithms.py` imports no driver
- Round-trip: dense index → Neo4j id → url is lossless

## Gotchas

- Only body links exist in `LINKS_TO` — the crawler discards nav, header, footer
  and sidebar at extraction, so no filtering is needed here.
- Two pages may link to each other. Decide whether that is one undirected edge or
  two, and be consistent — it changes degree counts.

**Depends on:** #3

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [08] PageRank and exact betweenness via igraph
body:
## Why

Betweenness is the most expensive algorithm in the pipeline at O(V·E). In-process
it runs exactly, which removes the sampling instability and the small-cluster
blind spot that sampling introduces.

```
PageRank        2-5s     damping 0.85
betweenness    60-190s   exact, all cores
```

## Steps

**a.** PageRank on the directed graph:
```python
pr = g_directed.pagerank(damping=0.85, weights=None)
```

**b.** Betweenness on the undirected graph:
```python
bc = g.betweenness()
```
Exact. Do not sample unless a measured runtime forces it — sampling is weakest at
exactly the thing betweenness is for, since a page bridging two *small* clusters
lies on few shortest paths overall.

**c.** Store betweenness as **percentile rank**, not raw value. Removes cross-run
magnitude drift and matches how trees consume it.

**d.** Write back in one batched `UNWIND`, chunked at ~5k rows.

**e.** ⚠️ **Correctness gate before trusting this.** Run the same graph through
GDS and igraph, compare:
```python
spearman(gds_pagerank, igraph_pagerank)   # must exceed 0.99
```
A fast wrong PageRank is worse than a slow right one.

**f.** Emit timings per algorithm so the runtime table can be replaced with
measurements.

## Acceptance

- Spearman vs GDS > 0.99 on the synthetic corpus
- Exact betweenness completes in under 4 minutes at 25k nodes
- Percentile ranks are stable across two identical runs

## Gotchas

- **This task may be deleted.** If `spearman(betweenness, pagerank) > 0.8` on real
  data, betweenness is redundant with PageRank and the whole stage comes out. See
  the Phase 2 gate.
- igraph's `pagerank` on a disconnected graph handles the teleport correctly, but
  isolated nodes still get a small nonzero value. Expected, not a bug.

**Depends on:** #7

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [09] Leiden ×2 via leidenalg: link graph and keyword graph
body:
## Why

Two clusterings answering two questions. The second is the cold-start fix and is
easy to skip by accident.

## Steps

**a.** Pass A over `LINKS_TO`:
```python
part = la.find_partition(g, la.RBConfigurationVertexPartition,
                         resolution_parameter=1.0, seed=42)
```
`RBConfiguration` rather than `Modularity` because it exposes a resolution
parameter for tuning cluster granularity. Write to `linkCommunityId`.

**b.** Pass B needs a **bipartite projection**. Build page↔keyword adjacency from
`TARGETS_KEYWORD`, then project to page-page — two pages are adjacent if they
target overlapping keywords, regardless of any link between them:
```cypher
MATCH (p:Page)-[:TARGETS_KEYWORD]->(k:Keyword)
RETURN id(p) AS page, id(k) AS keyword
```
Weight the projected edge by shared keyword count. Write to
`keywordCommunityId`.

**c.** Why Pass B exists: clustering pages by the links they already have is
circular. A new section has no links, so no cluster, so no recommendations —
precisely the pages that need help. Keyword relationships exist before any link
does.

**d.** Derive pillar and spoke per keyword cluster: pillar is the head term by
aggregate search volume, spokes are long-tail variants.

**e.** Fixed `seed=42` in development for reproducibility. In production consider
omitting it — a fixed seed hides genuine instability you would rather see.

**f.** Log per pass: community count, modularity, largest community as a fraction
of nodes, singleton count.

## Acceptance

- Both passes complete in under 20 seconds at 25k nodes
- Leiden guarantees connected communities; assert no community splits into
  multiple weakly-connected components
- On the synthetic corpus, ARI against planted topics exceeds 0.7

## Gotchas

- `largest_community_pct` above ~40% means the clustering is not discriminating.
  Log it and watch it.
- Leiden is order-dependent. Without a seed, cluster **ids** change between runs
  even when the partition is similar — never persist an id as a stable identifier.

**Depends on:** #7

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [10] HDBSCAN over content embeddings
body:
## Why

A third clustering answering a third question:
```
linkCommunityId      what is connected
keywordCommunityId   what we say it is about
hubId                what it is actually about
```

Its unique output is the `-1` noise label — a page belonging to no coherent topic.
Neither Leiden pass can express that, because Leiden must place every node
somewhere.

## Steps

**a.** Pull all `content_embedding` vectors into a NumPy array, ordered by the
same dense index used for the graph.

**b.** Cluster:
```python
cl = hdbscan.HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size=15, min_samples=None,
                     cluster_selection_method="eom", prediction_data=True)
labels = cl.fit_predict(X.astype(np.float64))
```
Try raw 2048d first. Only add UMAP if quality is poor — it pulls numba and adds a
second stochastic step with its own parameters.

**c.** Write `hubId`, with `-1` preserved as a real value rather than nulled.

**d.** Compute cluster centroids and store them. Needed by both hub-bridge scoring
and the pillar check.

**e.** ⚠️ **Cluster ids are unstable across runs.** If `hubId` feeds the model as
a categorical feature, match centroids between runs to keep ids stable, or the
feature is noise.

**f.** Log clusters found, noise count and fraction, largest cluster fraction, and
the condensed-tree depth.

## Acceptance

- On the synthetic corpus, the 24 planted noise pages are largely labelled `-1`
- Clusters recover the 5 planted topics, ARI > 0.6
- Runs in under 3 minutes at 25k pages

## Gotchas

- **This task may be deleted.** If `ARI(leiden, hdbscan) > 0.85` the two are
  duplicate features. See the Phase 2 gate.
- `min_cluster_size` too small fragments topics; too large merges them. 15 is a
  starting point, not a measured value.

**Depends on:** #5

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [11] GATE: clustering and betweenness evaluation
body:
## 🚦 Run before writing Phase 3. Two outcomes delete later work.

Half a day of measurement that can remove days of building. Do not skip it because
the code already exists.

## Steps

**a.** Seed the corpus and run the harnesses:
```bash
make seed
make eval              # ARI/NMI vs planted topics, noise P/R, purity
make eval-stability    # label churn across 4 runs
```

**b.** Apply the decision rules:
```
ARI(leiden, hdbscan) 0.3-0.7    keep both — they disagree usefully
                     > 0.85     DROP HDBSCAN, delete #10
noise_recall         < 0.5      HDBSCAN's main advantage failed
spearman(bc, pagerank) > 0.8    DELETE betweenness, remove from #8
```

**c.** Check label stability. Leiden with a fixed seed is reproducible; HDBSCAN
labels churn. Pairwise ARI below ~0.8 across runs means `hubId` needs centroid
matching before it can be a categorical feature — a real cost that appears in no
quality metric.

**d.** Check per-topic purity, not just aggregate ARI. This is where density
sensitivity shows: the corpus plants spreads from 0.18 to 0.55, and a global
resolution parameter cannot serve both equally.

**e.** Write the outcome into the wiki `Measurement-Backlog` with the numbers, not
just the conclusion. Future work needs to see what was measured.

## Acceptance

- Decision recorded with supporting numbers
- Any deleted work removed from the roadmap, not left as dead code
- Feature list for Phase 4 finalised

## Gotchas

- Synthetic embeddings are built to cluster cleanly. A good result here proves the
  plumbing works, not that clustering is good on real content.
- If everything scores near-perfectly, suspect the corpus is too easy rather than
  celebrating.

**Depends on:** #8, #9, #10

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [12] Candidate retrieval: hard constraints and HNSW
body:
## Why

Narrows an O(n²) pair space. The critical design point: **eligibility is not
priority**. Everything the old GSC filter decided is now a feature the ranker
weighs, and the ranker must see the candidates to learn their value.

## Steps

**a.** Eligibility is three constraints and nothing else:
```cypher
MATCH (t:Page) WHERE t.isIndexable = true
MATCH (s:Page) WHERE s.url <> t.url
  AND NOT (s)-[:LINKS_TO]->(t)
```

⚠️ **No GSC filter.** v3 required `impressions > 500 AND position 4-20`. Two
defects: `avg_position` is a mean over a heavily skewed query distribution, so a
page averaging 2.5 might rank #1 on five branded terms and #28 on forty commercial
ones. And it excluded new pages, orphans, striking-distance pages and pillars —
making hub-and-spoke unrepresentable.

**b.** HNSW top-50 per target:
```cypher
CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('page_gnn', 50, $target_vec)
YIELD node, score
```
Use `page_gnn` once GraphSAGE exists, `page_content` until then.

**c.** Apply hard constraints as a post-filter, and over-fetch (say 60) so
filtering still leaves 50.

**d.** Batch per target rather than per pair. 25k targets × 1 query, not 1.25M.

**e.** Emit candidate counts per target and total, plus the filter drop rate.

## Acceptance

- The 3 planted orphan NEW pages appear as candidate targets — if not, something
  is still filtering
- 25k targets complete in under 10 minutes
- No pair where a `LINKS_TO` already exists

## Gotchas

- Vector index queries return the query node itself. Exclude by id, not by score.
- Do not cap total candidates globally. Capping per target is correct; capping
  overall silently drops whole sections.

**Depends on:** #5, #9

**Estimate:** 1.5 days

title: [13] Jaccard signals: GSC query and strategic keyword overlap
body:
## Why

Both are set-against-set with **comparable sizes**, which is precisely Jaccard's
shape. The strategic keyword version is the cold-start-safe counterpart — it works
when neither page has GSC data yet.

## Steps

**a.** GSC query overlap:
```python
qa = {q.query for q in queries_for(source)}
qb = {q.query for q in queries_for(target)}
jaccard = len(qa & qb) / len(qa | qb) if (qa | qb) else 0.0
```
Null-safe: a new page has an empty set, which yields 0.0, not an error.

**b.** Strategic keyword overlap, same computation over `TARGETS_KEYWORD`. This
one works with zero GSC data, which is the whole point.

**c.** Both are **scoring inputs, not gates**. A pair with zero overlap still
proceeds — it just carries a weak signal.

**d.** Precompute query sets per URL once into a dict, rather than querying Mongo
per pair. 1.25M pairs × 2 Mongo round trips is not viable.

**e.** Add `keyword_gap`: keywords the page *targets* minus keywords it *ranks
for*. A large gap on a high-priority keyword is a strong signal the page needs
link support.

## Acceptance

- Pages with no GSC data score 0.0 rather than raising
- Precomputation means no per-pair database access
- Planted bridge-gap pairs show high query overlap despite near-zero link density

## Gotchas

- Normalise query strings before set operations — casing and whitespace.
- **Do not use cosine here.** These are sets of comparable size. Cosine is for the
  length-asymmetric cases in #16.

**Depends on:** #12

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [14] Cluster membership signals
body:
## Why

The three clusterings are only useful in combination. Their **disagreement** is
the signal, not any one of them alone.

## Steps

**a.** Attach `linkCommunityId`, `keywordCommunityId` and `hubId` for both source
and target, plus booleans for whether each matches.

**b.** Derive `cluster_agreement`:
```
same keyword + same link cluster       already well connected
same keyword + different link cluster  ← the missing link
different keyword + same link cluster  possibly a link to remove
```
Encode as a small categorical, not three separate booleans — the interaction is
what carries information.

**c.** Handle `hubId == -1` explicitly. Noise is a real category, not missing
data, and must not be treated as its own cluster in a match test.

**d.** If the Phase 2 gate dropped HDBSCAN, omit `hubId` here rather than passing
nulls.

## Acceptance

- **GATE:** the 3 planted orphan NEW pages appear as candidate targets with
  correct cluster ids
- `cluster_agreement` distribution is logged; the "missing link" bucket should be
  a meaningful minority, not near-zero or near-everything

## Gotchas

- Cluster ids are not stable across runs. These are per-run features, never
  persisted identifiers.

**Depends on:** #9, #10, #12

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [15] Feature assembly: ~30 context features
body:
## Why

This is what LambdaMART actually sees. Everything the removed GSC filter used to
decide is here as a feature.

## Feature groups

```
GSC          impressions_log, position_band (one-hot with NULL bucket),
             ctr_gap, has_gsc_data, query_count
lifecycle    stage one-hot, page_age_days
strategic    kw_count, max_priority, keyword_gap, pair_kw_overlap
target       inbound_count, is_orphan, crawl_depth, saturation_ratio
source       outbound_count, outbound_density, link_equity_share
cluster      linkCommunityId, keywordCommunityId, hubId, cluster_agreement
semantic     cosine(source, target), contextRelevance, anchorTargetFit
```

## Steps

**a.** `has_gsc_data` as an explicit boolean. Trees handle missingness better when
told about it than when it is imputed to zero.

**b.** `position_band` one-hot **with a NULL bucket**. A page that does not rank is
categorically different from one ranking at position 50.

**c.** `target_saturation_ratio` = actual inbound ÷ expected for its PageRank
tier. A pillar with 400 inbound links on a 5k-page site is saturated; one with 12
is under-linked regardless of how well it ranks. This expresses correctly what the
position filter was crudely gesturing at.

**d.** Source-side outbound features. Equity divides across a page's links, so a
page with 150 outbound links passes ~1/150 through each — a 151st is near
worthless. Nothing before v5 prevented recommending twenty new links on one page.
```
source_outbound_count
source_outbound_density     links per 1,000 words
source_link_equity_share    1 / (outbound_count + 1)
```

**e.** Assemble as a `pandas.DataFrame` with a stable column order, and persist
that order — LightGBM depends on positional consistency between train and predict.

**f.** ⚠️ **Chunk the assembly.** 1.25M pairs × 30 features is fine, but if this
later includes embeddings the memory ceiling arrives fast. Build the streaming
pattern now: assemble, score, discard in ~50k batches.

**g.** Cache the feature matrix to Parquet keyed by corpus hash. Recomputing on
every experiment iteration is wasteful.

## Acceptance

- Feature matrix for 1.25M pairs builds in under 45 minutes
- No column is entirely null or entirely constant
- Column order is deterministic across runs
- Memory stays bounded with chunking

## Gotchas

- Log-scale impressions. Raw values span orders of magnitude and dominate splits.
- `crawl_depth` comes from BFS over the crawl, not from the body-link graph — a
  page can be shallow via nav and unreachable via body links.

**Depends on:** #13, #14

**Estimate:** 2 days

title: [16] Cosine dimensions: contextRelevance and anchorTargetFit
body:
## Why

`anchorTargetFit` is the gap nothing else covers. `keywordAlignment` asks whether
the anchor contains the target's keyword — it cannot catch an anchor that matches
the keyword while the target page is about something else:

```
anchor:  "hydraulic press tonnage"          ← lexically fine
target:  page about press brake bending     ← wrong page entirely
```

## Steps

**a.** Compute both:
```python
contextRelevance = cosine(link.surroundingEmbedding, target.gnn_embedding)
anchorTargetFit  = cosine(anchor_embedding,          target.content_embedding)
```

**b.** ⚠️ **Both must be cosine, not Jaccard.** Length asymmetry: a 3-token anchor
against a 2,000-token page maxes out near 3/2000 ≈ 0.0015 on Jaccard, so every
score collapses into noise. Cosine treats both as directions in semantic space
regardless of length.

The rule that generalises:
```
comparable set sizes    → Jaccard    (query sets, keyword sets, anchor vs keyword)
length-asymmetric       → cosine     (anchor vs page, sentence vs page)
```

**c.** Use `vector.similarity.cosine()` in Cypher where both vectors are already
stored — avoids pulling them over the wire. Requires Neo4j 5.18+.

**d.** ⚠️ **Thresholds do not port across embedding models.** Local testing showed
0.75 flagging 2/3 test queries on Qwen and 0/3 on Voyage for identical content.
Re-derive for voyage-4-large; do not inherit a number from anywhere.

**e.** Log the distribution of both scores so thresholds can be set from data
rather than guessed.

## Acceptance

- Both bounded in [0,1] after normalisation
- 250k edges score in under 20 minutes
- Score distributions logged and visibly bimodal, not clustered at one end

## Gotchas

- `surroundingEmbedding` is on the relationship. There is no relationship vector
  index in Community, so this is a sequential scan — fine here, but do not attempt
  ANN over it.

**Depends on:** #6, #15

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [17] Hand-weighted linear scorer
body:
## Why

The baseline every later model must beat. Deliberately simple and legible — the
point is having something measurable before LambdaMART, not getting the weights
right.

## Steps

**a.** Normalise each feature to [0,1] with a documented method — min-max on
bounded features, percentile rank on heavy-tailed ones like PageRank.

**b.** Weighted sum with weights in config, not code, so they can be swept without
a deploy.

**c.** Scale to `opportunity_score` 0–100 and assign tiers (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) by
percentile within the run, not absolute cutoffs.

**d.** Emit per-recommendation the top three contributing features and their
values. This is what makes the output explainable and what you will read during
threshold tuning.

**e.** Persist scores so the NDCG harness in #26 can compare against them.

## Acceptance

- Scores span the full 0–100 range, not clustered
- Contribution breakdown appears on every recommendation
- Deterministic: same input, same score

## Gotchas

- These weights encode your priors. That is fine and expected — just do not
  mistake a good synthetic result for validation.

**Depends on:** #15, #16

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [18] Hub-to-hub bridge scoring
body:
## Why

Produces a handful of high-leverage **structural** recommendations rather than
thousands of page-level ones. Two topics that share search demand but have almost
no links between them is a strategic finding, not a per-page one.

## Steps

**a.** Score every cluster pair:
```python
bridge_gap = (0.4 * cosine(centroid_a, centroid_b)
            + 0.6 * jaccard(queries_a, queries_b)
            - link_density * 50)
```
Query Jaccard is weighted higher than semantic similarity because shared *demand*
is stronger evidence than shared vocabulary.

**b.** `link_density` = cross-cluster links ÷ (size_a × size_b). The ×50 scaling
puts it on a comparable range to the other terms — tune it against real data.

**c.** For the top-ranked pairs, pick the best page pair: source with highest
centrality and outbound capacity, target closest to the source cluster's centroid.

**d.** Emit as its own recommendation type with cluster sizes and the shared
queries that justify it.

## Acceptance

- **GATE:** both planted bridge gaps rank in the top 3 by `bridge_gap`. They have
  3 and 5 cross-links against ≥57 for every other pair, so the signal is clean if
  the scoring is right.
- Well-connected pairs rank near the bottom

## Gotchas

- Requires `hubId` from #10. If the Phase 2 gate dropped HDBSCAN, this can run on
  `keywordCommunityId` instead — note the substitution in the output.
- The ×50 constant is a guess. Log the three terms separately so it can be tuned.

**Depends on:** #10, #13

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [19] Keyword resolution chain
body:
## Why

Determines what the anchor is *for*. Getting this wrong degrades every anchor
downstream, and v4's version had a defect inherited from the removed GSC filter.

## Steps

**a.** Resolution order:
```
1  strategic primary keyword          if assigned
2  highest-opportunity GSC query      see below
3  extracted from title / h1          last resort
```

**b.** ⚠️ **GSC selection is by opportunity value, not position band.** v4 took the
top query where the target ranked 5–20 — the same defect as the removed Step ④
filter, relocated. A page at position 3 on a high-value commercial term still
needs links to reach 1.
```python
opportunity_value = impressions * (ctr_at_1 - ctr_at_current)
```
Estimated click upside. Favours high-demand terms wherever they rank, and
deprioritises positions 1–2 naturally where upside is near zero — no hard cutoff.

**c.** The CTR curve comes from **#36**, derived per tenant. Do not use an industry
table; curves differ substantially by vertical and SERP feature mix.

**d.** Title/h1 fallback: strip brand suffixes and boilerplate before using.

**e.** Record which rung produced the keyword. Needed to diagnose poor anchors
later.

**f.** The two sources disagree usefully — a page targeting "industrial hydraulic
press" but ranking for "press machine repair" is a content gap, captured as
`keyword_gap`.

## Acceptance

- Pages with a strategic primary always use it
- Pages with no GSC data fall through to title without error
- Rung distribution logged across the corpus

## Gotchas

- Every page in the synthetic corpus has a strategic keyword, so rungs 2 and 3 are
  barely exercised there. Test them explicitly with fixtures.

**Depends on:** #3

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [20] Extraction ladder rungs 1-2
body:
## Why

Anchor text is a ranking signal, not a copywriting problem. The keyword is the
specification and the operation is **extraction** — find where the topic is
already mentioned and link that phrase. That is what an SEO does by hand; you do
not rewrite the client's copy.

## Steps

**a.** Rung 1, exact match. Case-insensitive, whitespace-normalised, word-boundary
aware so "press" does not match inside "pressure". Return the phrase with its
character offsets — the caller needs to know *where*.

**b.** Rung 2, stemmed variant:
```python
from nltk.stem.snowball import SnowballStemmer
stem = SnowballStemmer(LANG_MAP[page.language]).stem
```
⚠️ **Key off `page.language`, not hardcoded English.** Snowball ships ~15
languages and tenants are multilingual. Cheap now, painful to retrofit once
English is assumed throughout.

Handles plurals, `-ing`, `-ed`, and modifier drop ("industrial hydraulic press" →
"hydraulic press").

**c.** Sentence-split the body first, so a match returns its containing sentence
for context.

**d.** If several sentences match, prefer earlier ones — link prominence within
the copy is a real signal.

**e.** Return a structured result: matched phrase, rung, sentence, offsets. Never
a bare string.

## Acceptance

- Pages containing their head term verbatim resolve at rung 1
- Plural and `-ing` forms resolve at rung 2
- Non-English pages use the correct stemmer
- No match inside a larger word

## Gotchas

- Do not stem the whole document up front — expensive and destroys offsets. Stem
  the keyword and candidate phrases only.

**Depends on:** #19

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [21] Rung 2.5: Jaccard on stemmed token sets
body:
## Why

Sits between stemmed matching and embedding cosine, and saves the expensive rung.

```
keyword:  "industrial hydraulic press"
phrase:   "hydraulic press systems"

rung 2    may miss — different token count
rung 3    catches it, costs an embedding call
rung 2.5  jaccard on stemmed sets = 0.5 → free
```

Rung 3 embeds candidate noun phrases **per pair**, so anything diverted before it
is a direct saving.

## Steps

**a.** Extract candidate noun-ish phrases per sentence — 2–5 word windows is
sufficient without a POS tagger.

**b.** Stem both sides, compare as sets:
```python
jaccard = len(kw_stems & phrase_stems) / len(kw_stems | phrase_stems)
```

**c.** Threshold at 0.5 initially. Sweep 0.3–0.7 and measure what fraction of
rung-3 hits this diverts and whether it introduces bad matches.

**d.** Both sides are short and comparable in size, which is why Jaccard is
correct here — unlike #16 where the asymmetry demands cosine.

**e.** Log the divert rate. Worth keeping if it takes more than ~20% of rung-3
traffic without false positives.

## Acceptance

- Diverts a measurable fraction of rung-3 traffic
- False-positive rate stays low across the threshold sweep
- Threshold is config, not a literal

## Gotchas

- Very short keywords (one token) make Jaccard degenerate — either 0 or 1. Skip
  this rung for single-token keywords.

**Depends on:** #20

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [22] Rung 3: semantic phrase match with caching
body:
## Why

The last resort before `CONTENT_GAP`, and the expensive one — it embeds candidate
phrases per pair.

## Steps

**a.** Extract candidate noun phrases. spaCy if the `nlp` extra is installed,
otherwise the 2–5 word windows from #21.

**b.** Embed candidates and compare to `target.gnn_embedding`. Threshold ~0.62 as
a starting point.

**c.** ⚠️ **Cache aggressively** by `(source_url, content_hash)`. The same source
page appears across many pairs, and its candidate phrases do not change between
them. Without this the cost is unbounded.

**d.** Cap candidates per sentence — 10 is plenty. Embedding every n-gram is
wasteful.

**e.** ⚠️ **Re-derive the threshold for voyage-4-large.** 0.62 was derived against
different embeddings and absolute cosine values do not port between models.

**f.** Log rung-3 invocation count and cache hit rate. If the hit rate is low, the
cache key is wrong.

## Acceptance

- Cache hit rate above 80% on a full run
- Threshold derived from the corpus, not inherited
- Rung 3 fires on a minority of pairs

## Gotchas

- Rung 3 returning a phrase with zero lexical overlap is legitimate — that is the
  point of a semantic rung. But log those cases; they are the ones most likely to
  read oddly.

**Depends on:** #20, #6

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [23] Anchor scoring and type distribution
body:
## Why

Picks between candidates and keeps the inbound anchor profile healthy without ever
blocking a good link.

## Steps

**a.** Four weighted dimensions:
```
semantic   .35    cosine(anchor, target.gnn_embedding)
keyword    .35    0.7 * jaccard(stemmed) + 0.3 * cosine
diversity  .15    JACCARD vs existing inbound anchors — not cosine
length     .15    optimal 2-4 words
```

**b.** ⚠️ **Diversity must be Jaccard.** Over-optimisation is about repeating
*words*. Cosine rates "commercial press machine" as non-diverse against
"industrial hydraulic press" at 0.85; Jaccard correctly gives 0.20.

**c.** Naturalness was **removed**. It existed to catch awkward LLM phrasing, and
an extracted phrase already reads naturally in its own sentence — that is what
made it extractable. This also removes the LLM-as-judge self-preference bias.

**d.** Type distribution (15 exact / 20 partial / 50 natural / 15 branded): count
the target's existing inbound anchors by type, prefer whichever is
underrepresented.

**e.** ⚠️ **Ordering matters and was ambiguous in v4.** Extraction runs first. The
profile only chooses *between candidates that already exist in the copy*. If the
sole available phrase is a partial match, use it even when the profile wants
exact. Never skip a good link because a ratio preferred something else.

**f.** Profile is per-tenant config. The 15/20/50/15 figures are conventional SEO
heuristics, not measured.

## Acceptance

- **GATE:** extraction succeeds on ~78% of pages and falls through on ~22%, within
  ±5%. Check against `db.pages.find({_planted: "NO_HEAD_TERM"})`.
- Diversity penalises literal repetition, not semantic similarity
- A partial-only page still produces a link

## Gotchas

- Type classification needs the keyword. An anchor is EXACT relative to a specific
  keyword, not in the abstract.

**Depends on:** #22

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [24] Proxy label generation
body:
## Why

LambdaMART trains on acceptance labels. On synthetic data nobody has accepted
anything, so labels come from planted structure.

## Steps

**a.** Assign graded labels:
```python
label = 3  if pair spans a planted BRIDGE_GAP
        3  if target is a planted ORPHAN_NEW_STRATEGIC page
        2  if source and target share keywordCommunityId
        1  if target is TRUE_NOISE          # should rank low
        0  otherwise
```

**b.** Group by source page — LambdaMART ranks *within* a group, so grouping must
match how recommendations are consumed.

**c.** Balance check: if label 3 is under ~1% of pairs the model has almost nothing
to learn from. Log the distribution.

**d.** Hold out 20% by **source page**, not by pair. Splitting pairs leaks — the
same source appears on both sides.

**e.** ⚠️ **State the limitation in the output.** This validates plumbing and
feature engineering, not ranking quality. A model that learns these perfectly has
learned *your priors*.

## Acceptance

- Label distribution logged and non-degenerate
- Holdout split is by source page with no overlap
- Reproducible from a seed

## Gotchas

- Do not use features to derive labels. Labelling on `keywordCommunityId` and
  *also* feeding it as a feature makes that feature trivially predictive and the
  evaluation meaningless. Either drop the feature or drop that label rule.

**Depends on:** #15

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [25] LightGBM lambdarank
body:
## Why

Ranking rather than regression because traffic delta is not attributable to a
single link — confounded by algorithm updates, seasonality, content changes.
Acceptance is directly observable.

## Steps

**a.** Configure:
```python
params = dict(objective="lambdarank", metric="ndcg", ndcg_eval_at=[10],
              learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31,
              min_data_in_leaf=20, feature_fraction=0.8)
```

**b.** `group` array must be the count of rows per source page, in the same order
as the data. This is the most common LightGBM ranking mistake and it fails
silently — you get a model, just a meaningless one.

**c.** Early stopping on validation NDCG@10, 50 rounds patience.

**d.** Persist the feature column order alongside the model. LightGBM depends on
positional consistency between train and predict.

**e.** Export feature importance by gain, not split count. Split count rewards
high-cardinality features regardless of usefulness.

**f.** Chunked inference from the start — assemble, score, discard in ~50k
batches. At 2048d the pair vector roughly doubles, so the memory ceiling arrives
sooner than earlier estimates suggested.

## Acceptance

- Trains without error on the synthetic corpus
- NDCG@10 improves over training rounds
- Feature importance is non-degenerate — no single feature above ~60% gain
- Inference on 1.25M pairs stays within memory

## Gotchas

- A single feature dominating usually means label leakage. Check #24's gotcha.
- `min_data_in_leaf=20` is high for small label counts. Lower it for early runs
  and raise it as labels accumulate.

**Depends on:** #24

**Estimate:** 1.5 days

title: [26] NDCG@10 harness: baseline vs learned
body:
## Why

**The gate.** If the learned model does not beat a hand-weighted linear scorer,
the features are the problem, not the model — and no amount of tuning fixes that.

## Steps

**a.** Score the same holdout with both #17 and #25.

**b.** Compute NDCG@10 per source group, then average. Report the distribution,
not just the mean — a good average hiding many zero-scoring groups is a different
situation from uniform mediocrity.

**c.** ⚠️ **Log `n_labelled_pairs` alongside every NDCG figure.** With few labels
the metric is noise: grouped by source page, most groups have one or two graded
items and the rest zeros. The number must never be read without its sample size.

**d.** Also report precision@5 and the fraction of groups with any label above 0 —
NDCG alone hides sparsity.

**e.** Bootstrap a confidence interval over source groups. A 0.02 improvement with
a 0.08 interval is not an improvement.

## Acceptance

- Both scorers evaluated identically
- CI reported alongside the point estimate
- Result written into the wiki with numbers

## Gotchas

- NDCG needs a graded relevance scale. Binary labels make it degenerate to
  something close to MAP.

**Depends on:** #17, #25

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [27] MLflow tracking and feature importance report
body:
## Why

Feature importance is **the real output of this phase**. It answers three
measurement-backlog questions at once.

## Steps

**a.** Point at the existing MLflow server. Log params, metrics, the model
artefact, feature importance, and the label distribution.

**b.** Tag runs with corpus size, seed, feature set version and git SHA. Without
these, comparing runs later is guesswork.

**c.** Log feature importance as an artefact, not just a metric, so it is
inspectable.

**d.** Read the outcomes:
```
betweenness low        → delete #8, saves 60-190s/run
hubId low              → HDBSCAN was a duplicate, drop #10
keyword_gap high       → strategic keyword work paid off
saturation_ratio high  → outbound features earned their place
```

**e.** Promotion gate is a **registry stage transition**, not application logic. A
version moves to Production only if it beats the current Production NDCG@10 on
holdout.

**f.** Block promotion from local runs. Only CI transitions stages.

## Acceptance

- Runs appear in MLflow with full tags
- Feature importance retrievable as an artefact
- Promotion gate rejects a worse model

## Gotchas

- MLflow's artefact store is MinIO. Verify `MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL` is set or
  artefact logging fails with an unhelpful boto3 error.

**Depends on:** #25

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [28] Run real crawl through the full pipeline
body:
## Why

First contact with real content. Settles three things synthetic data structurally
cannot.

## Steps

**a.** Ingest one real crawl into a separate tenant so synthetic and real never
mix.

**b.** Full pipeline end to end, timing every stage. Compare against the runtime
projections — every number in the wiki is an estimate until this runs.

**c.** Measure **extraction hit rate** per rung. The 78% synthetic figure is a
generator property, not a fact about the web. This determines `CONTENT_GAP` volume
and how much opportunity is actionable without writing new content.

**d.** Measure **fixable-link rate**: verdicts emitted ÷ total edges.
```
< 10%   audit is a feature, discovery is the product
> 30%   the audit IS the product
```
This drives the roadmap split.

**e.** Sanity-read 20 recommendations. Not a metric — a smell test. Anything
obviously wrong here means a bug, not a tuning problem.

**f.** Note embedding behaviour on real text: boilerplate, inconsistent lengths,
navigation remnants that survived extraction.

## Acceptance

- Pipeline completes without manual intervention
- Both rates measured and recorded
- Stage timings replace the projections in the wiki

## Gotchas

- Real crawls have redirect chains, duplicate content and pagination the synthetic
  corpus lacks. Expect ingestion bugs here, not algorithm bugs.

**Depends on:** #23, #26

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [29] Stratified sampling and blind label export
body:
## Why

How the labels are drawn determines whether the evaluation means anything.

## Steps

**a.** Sample ~200 pairs **stratified by score decile**, roughly 20 per decile.

⚠️ **Do not take the top 200.** Labelling only high scorers means the model never
sees negatives and learns nothing about what to reject. The bottom deciles need
labelling precisely to confirm they belong there.

**b.** Export to CSV **without scores, ranks or any model output**. Columns:
source url, target url, proposed anchor, the sentence it sits in, target title.

**c.** Shuffle before export. Ordering leaks the ranking.

**d.** Label as accept / modify / dismiss. Modify means the link is wanted but the
anchor needs changing — a partial win, and it maps to label 2.

**e.** Join back on a random id, not on position.

**f.** ⚠️ **Label blind.** Labelling with the score visible anchors you to it and
makes the evaluation circular.

## Acceptance

- Export has no model output in any column
- Every decile represented
- Join is verifiable and lossless

## Gotchas

- 200 labels from one person is directionally sound but a sample of one. State it
  in the write-up so a strong NDCG is not read as validated against the
  profession.

**Depends on:** #28

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [30] Retrain on real labels, holdout NDCG@10
body:
## 🚦 The gate that answers "does the intelligence core work."

Everything before this validates plumbing.

## Steps

**a.** Map labels: accept → 3, modify → 2, dismiss → 1, unlabelled → 0.

**b.** Train on ~150, hold out ~50, split by source page.

**c.** Compare three scorers on the same holdout: hand-weighted baseline,
proxy-label model from #25, and the real-label model.

**d.** The proxy-vs-real comparison is informative in itself. If the proxy model
performs near-randomly on real labels, the planted structure did not reflect real
judgement — worth knowing before trusting any synthetic result again.

**e.** Report feature importance from the real-label model and diff it against the
proxy one. Features that matter for real judgement but not for planted structure
are the interesting ones.

**f.** 200 labels will **not** support GraphSAGE — the extra capacity overfits long
before it helps. Do not read a poor result as evidence against the GNN.

## Acceptance

- Learned model beats the heuristic baseline on held-out real labels
- Bootstrap CI reported
- Proxy-vs-real importance diff recorded

## Gotchas

- If real-label NDCG is barely above the baseline, the honest conclusion is that
  ~30 tabular features carry most of the available signal — which is useful, and
  argues against building the GNN.

**Depends on:** #29

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [31] End-to-end runs at three scales
body:
## Steps

**a.** Run at 600, 5,000 and 25,000 pages, logging duration per stage.

**b.** Compare against the projections. Betweenness grows O(V·E), so 5k is ~70×
the work of 600 — the place scaling assumptions break first.

**c.** Watch peak memory at 25k, particularly during feature assembly and
LambdaMART inference.

**d.** Verify the parallel schedule actually overlaps: graph analytics and audit
pass A should run inside the embedding window, not after it.

**e.** Update the Architecture runtime table with measured numbers and delete the
"provisional" note.

## Acceptance

- All three complete
- Measured timings replace projections
- Peak memory stays within a 32 GB node at 25k

## Gotchas

- 25k pages against the real Voyage API costs real money and takes ~28 minutes.
  Run it once, not iteratively.

**Depends on:** #30

**Estimate:** 0.5 days

title: [32] Ground truth assertion suite
body:
## Why

Turns "it seems to work" into a pass/fail board that runs in CI.

## The ten checks

```
Synthetic
 1  clusters recover 5 planted topics        ARI vs _topic > 0.7
 2  24 noise pages excluded or flagged       noise_recall > 0.6
 3  3 orphan NEW pages surface as ADD_LINK   all in top decile
 4  2 bridge gaps rank top by hub score      both in top 3 pairs
 5  2 pillar mismatches caught               centroid-nearest != declared
 6  extraction ~78% hit, ~22% fallthrough    within ±5%
 7  learned ranker beats heuristic           NDCG@10 improvement

Real crawl
 8  extraction hit rate on real content      measured, not asserted
 9  fixable-link rate                        measured, not asserted
10  ranker beats baseline on real labels     the actual gate
```

## Steps

**a.** Implement 1–7 as pytest tests against a seeded corpus, marked `slow`.

**b.** Implement 8–10 as a reporting script, not assertions — they measure rather
than gate, and the right threshold is unknown until measured.

**c.** Each failure message must state expected, actual, and which planted fixture
it refers to.

**d.** Run the suite in CI nightly, not per PR — it needs a seeded corpus and real
embeddings.

## Acceptance

- All seven synthetic checks pass
- Three real-crawl measurements recorded
- Failures are diagnosable from the message alone

## Gotchas

- Checks 1–7 depend on the corpus seed. Pin it, and re-verify after any generator
  change.

**Estimate:** 1 day

title: [33] Feature importance report and decision write-up
body:
## Why

Close the loop. Several measurement-backlog items are now answerable, and the ones
that are not need stating explicitly so a green board is not over-read.

## Steps

**a.** Close out the backlog items this build settled, with numbers.

**b.** Record the deletions: did betweenness survive? HDBSCAN? Remove dead code,
do not leave it behind a flag.

**c.** Write the "does not prove" section:
```
generalisation beyond one site     one real crawl, one content style
labeller agreement                 200 labels, one person
2048 vs 1024                       untested for full-page doc-to-doc
                                   comparison with voyage-4-large
long-page dilution                 chunking deferred, every page is one vector
```

**d.** Decide on Phase 7 of the wider roadmap — GraphSAGE and cross-attention —
using the #30 result. If ~30 tabular features carry most of the signal, that is a
strong argument against 19 more days.

**e.** Update Architecture, Decisions and Measurement-Backlog so the wiki reflects
what was built rather than what was planned.

## Acceptance

- Every backlog item either closed with numbers or restated with a plan
- Deleted components removed from wiki and code
- Next-phase decision recorded with its justification

## Gotchas

- The temptation is to declare success. The more useful artefact is a precise list
  of what remains unknown.
